findings.title: The ConfigError→exit 2 arm sits at main()'s outermost catch, so a config the TOOL just wrote is reported as the user's bad config, without a backtrace
locations: src/CLI/Main.jl:147-151 (the new arm in main()'s catch)
src/CLI/Init.jl:565 — `cfg = Config.read(root; check = false)` after `init(root; io)` wrote the config
test/coverage.jl:8-30 — the `the exit contract of main()` testset, in this change set, gains no case for the new branch
findings.before:
catch err
        println(stderr, "gbg ", key, ": crashed — ", sprint(showerror, err))
        Base.show_backtrace(stderr, catch_backtrace()); println(stderr)
        return 3
findings.after: err isa Config.ConfigError && (println(stderr, "gbg ", key, ": ", sprint(showerror, err)); return 2)
findings.why_it_matters: The stated defect is narrow: `Config.read` at a verb's ENTRY throws on a hand-edited config, and only three verbs (cmd_config, cmd_doctor, design_verb) mapped that to the documented exit 2. The edit fixes it at the outermost frame instead, so it also swallows a ConfigError raised anywhere else in a verb's body. Two such sites are in the tree today: `gbg bump` writes the new pin into .gbg/config.toml and THEN calls `Config.read(root)` (Bump.jl:36), and `gbg new` calls `Config.read(root; check = false)` on the config `init` just rendered (Init.jl:565). If the tool renders a config it cannot read back — a template defect, a bad substitution, a path the renderer got wrong — the operator now sees `gbg bump: config error: …` and exit 2, "cannot evaluate", the same line a hand-edited config produces, with the half-rewritten config.toml left on disk and the backtrace (the only thing naming Bump.jl:36 as the frame) discarded. Exit 3 existed to say "this is the tool's fault, here is where"; that signal is now unavailable for the whole ConfigError class, and CLAUDE.md makes exit codes the contract a log is never grepped to replace. Narrowing the catch to the config-read boundary — or to verbs that have written nothing yet — would fix the stated defect without covering the post-write reads.
findings.description: The underlying fix is right: a structurally bad consumer config is exit 2 by D8, and most verbs reported it as a crash. But the edit is wider than that defect. Placed in main()'s catch-all it cannot distinguish a ConfigError thrown before the verb did anything from one thrown after the verb rewrote the consumer's config, and it deletes the backtrace for both. The two post-write re-reads (Bump.jl:36, Init.jl:565) are exactly the case where exit 3 carried information nothing else carries. No test was added: the testset that owns main()'s exit contract is itself in this change set and enumerates the other exit codes case by case, so the new branch is the one arm of that contract with no oracle.
findings.evidence: Main.jl:147-151 comment: "`Config.read` throws it, and only three verbs caught it themselves, so every other verb reported a hand-edited config.toml as exit 3. Catching the class once here fixes it for all." — the rationale names `Config.read` at entry, but the arm is placed around `return Int(VERBS[key](rest))`, i.e. the whole verb. Bump.jl:34-36: `write(p, new)` / `cfg2 = Config.read(root)`. test/coverage.jl:8-16 asserts `G.main(["probe","--fail"]) == 2`, `G.main(["no-such-verb"]) == 2`, `G.main(String[]) == 2` — and nothing for a ConfigError.

findings.title: Two guards the design promised are withdrawn from the contract rather than built, with the code left exactly as it was
locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1447-1448 (§6.1 file formats) — the classification list
IMPLEMENTATION.md:403 (step 1.6, outside the audit's covered paths) — the same list
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1979-1986 (§8 step-0 `gbg round import`) — the `self verify` promise
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:470-490 (bank iterates the roster) and 736-757 (`import_empty`) — unchanged
findings.before: An **ORPHAN** (a lane file no roster entry expects) is reported, never counted. … It needs no `.gbg/config.toml` — the one `round` verb that runs before `init`; `self verify` still precedes it — and refuses (exit 2) an existing target round
findings.after: A lane file no roster entry expects is not classified at all: `bank` iterates the roster, so a stray file in `findings/` is neither read nor reported. … which the CLI does not yet allow, since `cmd_round` reads the config before dispatching any round verb, and the implemented `--empty` path calls neither `guard` nor `self verify`, unlike every other round verb.
findings.why_it_matters: Both edits resolve a doc-vs-code mismatch in the direction of the code, and both mismatches were a missing guard. (1) ORPHAN: a lane agent that writes findings/04-under-rejection.json when the roster expects 03 has its findings silently discarded — bank never opens the file, and the only signal is the roster entry going DEAD, which `gbg round rerun` then re-runs over the top of the orphan. The design said that file is "reported"; the head text says it is "neither read nor reported", and the sentence now reads as intent rather than as the debt it is. (2) import_empty: it is the one round verb that writes into .gbg/rounds/ with no self_verify (running copy ≠ pinned copy) and no torn_check/config_sha guard — verified at Rounds.jl:736-757, where the only refusals are the round-id regex, a 12-character reason and an existing directory. The base text asserted `self verify` still precedes it; the head text records that it does not and stops there. Per the package's own RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK, a rule whose check is deleted rather than paid is a weakness, not an answer — neither withdrawal is accompanied by a check, a ledger entry or a WORK_QUEUE item in this change set.
findings.description: One class, two instances: a guard the base contract promised is deleted from the contract, the code is untouched, and the head prose presents the unguarded state as the design. Bringing stale prose current is right in general; here the stale prose was the only record that a guard was owed, so the edit converts an unpaid debt into a settled fact. The ORPHAN withdrawal also spans IMPLEMENTATION.md, which lies outside this audit's covered paths, so one member of the class would not have been visible to a lane reading only the covered diff.
findings.evidence: Base ARCHITECTURE.md:616 "An **ORPHAN** (a lane file no roster entry expects) is reported, never counted."; base IMPLEMENTATION.md:403 "classes DEAD/EMPTY/ORPHAN/TRUNCATED/REJECTED (D10)" → head "classes DEAD/EMPTY/TRUNCATED/REJECTED (D10 — bank iterates the roster, so a lane file no roster entry expects is not classified at all)". Rounds.jl:736-757: `function import_empty(...)` contains no call to `guard(` or `self_verify(`, unlike `guard` at Rounds.jl:66-72 which every other round verb routes through.

findings.title: The prose-shape ratchet is re-recorded in the same commit as the growth it would have caught, and one paragraph crosses the rule's own 120-word cap under cover of it
locations: docs/prose_shape.csv — §7.3 1979→2044, §8 1521→1615, §12.A, §12.B, §1, §6.1, §6.8, item 2, config.md, install.md, ledger.md, rounds.md, Passes::Passes 223→303, Passes::close, Preflight::torn_check 43→107, Rounds::Rounds (18 rows raised, 1 added)
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:643-646 — the §D11 paragraph the raised row covers
src/Scans/prose_shape.jl:95-120 (the ratchet and the cap gate)
findings.before: "ARCHITECTURE.md § D11 — Schemas: one JSON Schema per artefact kind in `schema/",124,80,0
findings.after: "ARCHITECTURE.md § D11 — Schemas: one JSON Schema per artefact kind in `schema/",170,126,0
findings.why_it_matters: RULE.DOC.SHAPE's 120-word paragraph cap does not bind on a baselined page unit — src/Scans/prose_shape.jl gates it as `if occursin(" :: ", k) || b === nothing`, so for these ARCHITECTURE sections the ratchet IS the whole of the check. Raising the row in the same commit as the prose therefore removes the only constraint those units have. D11 is the decisive one: its longest paragraph goes 80→126 words, over the rule's stated cap, because a ~55-word clause was appended to an existing paragraph — precisely what the scan's own hit text tells the author not to do ("rewrite, do not append; re-baseline deliberately if the growth is new content"). A reader of the CSV afterwards cannot tell which of the 18 raised rows were considered and which came along with the regeneration, since `write_prose_shape_baseline` rewrites every row from the current tree.
findings.description: The policy does sanction a deliberate re-record (docs-rubric.md: "the shape baseline is re-recorded deliberately, never by accident"), and every raised row does map to a file this diff edits — I checked, and no row was lowered or removed, so this is not a blanket reset hiding unrelated drift. What remains is that the guard and the growth land in one commit with nothing recording the deliberation, and that one unit now sits above the absolute cap the rule states, reachable only because the ratchet was the sole check on it and the ratchet was moved. The cheap discipline the rule implies — rewrite the D11 paragraph instead of appending to it — would have kept the row where it was.
findings.evidence: src/Scans/prose_shape.jl: `(u.words > w || u.longest > l || u.admonitions > a) && push!(hits, Hit(file, 0, "$k GREW: … — rewrite, do not append; re-baseline deliberately if the growth is new content"))`, and the cap gate `if occursin(" :: ", k) || b === nothing`. ARCHITECTURE.md:643-646 inserts "lane-file wrapper, whose findings array `$ref`s a REDUCED `$defs.finding` local to that file — … which is why the instrument file cannot simply `$ref` it." into the existing paragraph.
